messages:
ravi: quick drop: I've put together a compact preflight+acceptance flow for model onboarding. goal: surface interface/compat issues fast and keep bench costs bounded. sketch below.
emma: nice, want to see the sketch.
jon: +1, especially interested in how we treat quant artifacts.
ravi: sketch:
```
preflight (cheap):
  - descriptor_lint: schema + required fields (owner, ops_list, quant_profile)
  - tokenizer_check: tokenizer hash vs manifest
  - micro_bench: 12 stratified samples (short, mid, long) perf + accuracy probes
  - compat_smoke: ops_list vs runtime_supported_ops (fast)
  - kv_prefix_smoke: synthetic cache hits (local sandbox)
acceptance (heavier):
  - full_bench: 1k samples (statistical buckets)
  - quant_checksum: artifact.fingerprint -> verify reproduces golden FP on subset
  - staged_rollout: 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 1% with health gates
```
notes: micro_bench is meant to be deterministic (golden-capped inputs) so we fail-fast on big regressions.
jon: I like synthetic kv smoke in preflight so we don't hit prod caches. can we run it inside the intake sandbox?
tara: yes, but we should still have an optional live-kv check in acceptance for real-world cache semantics.
emma: agree. also propose a tiny eval (micro_eval) in preflight: 20 golden prompts measuring rough LL/EM to catch big accuracy regressions. opt-in for >2GB models.
ravi: good call. mapping of signals -> block/warn/info (proposal):
  - BLOCK: tokenizer mismatch, missing required ops, checksum mismatch on manifest or quant artifact, runtime-crash on micro_bench
  - WARN: median perf drop 5%+, memory +10%, small accuracy delta on micro_eval (> threshold)
  - INFO: tail latency jitter, <2x baseline, small numerical drift on outputs
jon: we need explicit numeric thresholds in a central policy file so admit-bot can evaluate.
emma: and owner routing: descriptor must include onboard-owner label (email/Slack handle). block failures auto-notify owner + #eng-ml-onboard.
ravi: admit-bot events example: `admit-bot: {`
